Divergence: reference TaskDefinitionAwsVpc.py:61-75 checks NetworkMode with the top-level validator and then iterates port mappings with that same validator (_get_port_mappings(validator, instance)). It therefore reports a HostPort/ContainerPort mismatch regardless of which NetworkMode branch is awsvpc.

Generated patch.diff:254-265 instead builds scoped_validator from network_mode_validator (the awsvpc branch's condition context) and iterates port mappings with it, so ports are narrowed to the NetworkMode branch's conditions.

Runtime check (/tmp/judge-3546-scratch/run_case.py, run with -B -I): Case A (NetworkMode = Fn::If[IsProd,'awsvpc','bridge']; HostPort = Fn::If[IsProd,8080,80]; ContainerPort 8080) gives reference [('80 does not equal 8080', ...)] and generated []. Case B (unconditional awsvpc, HostPort 80) gives the same single error in both. Case C (ServiceNetworkConfiguration with conditional NetworkMode) gives the same single required error in both.

The reference tests do not cover conditional NetworkMode, so they pass; the divergence is only visible on conditional templates. The generated output is arguably more precise, but the reference is the source of truth for behavior, so this is a behavioral mismatch.

Parity elsewhere: ServiceFargate produced identical output in both trees for four edge cases, including a conditional LaunchType, Fn::GetAtt as a list and as a string, and a conditional TaskDefinition (run_fargate.py).
criteria.deficiency: TaskDefinitionAwsVpc (patch.diff:254-265) narrows port-mapping evaluation to the condition scope of the awsvpc NetworkMode branch, whereas the reference (reference TaskDefinitionAwsVpc.py:61-75) evaluates ports under the outer scope. For conditional NetworkMode, the patch suppresses a '... does not equal ...' error that the reference reports (verified by Case A). This is a narrow case with no reference-test or fixture coverage, but it is an observable behavioral difference. Making the generated code match the reference would mean iterating ports with the outer validator. Minor non-failing note: ServiceFargate's Fn::GetAtt parsing (patch.diff:46-49) is more defensive than the reference (reference ServiceFargate.py:43), which would raise on an empty or non-string first element; this is an improvement, not a regression.
